paraphrase: Salutation to Kṛṣṇa, whose form is being, consciousness and bliss, who acts without effort, who is known through Vedānta, the guru and the witness of the intellect.
'Kṛṣ' denotes existence and 'ṇa' bliss; their union is Kṛṣṇa, the supreme Brahman.

checks.note: The opening of the Gopālapūrvatāpanī is located: 'kṛṣir bhūvācakaḥ śabdo ṇaś ca nirvṛtivācakaḥ | tayor aikyaṃ paraṃ brahma kṛṣṇa ity abhidhīyate'.

paraphrase: The sages ask Brahmā who is the supreme god, whom death fears; Brahmā: Kṛṣṇa (Govinda) is the supreme god; his meditation form and his mantra are given.

checks.note: Located in the first upaniṣat of the pūrva: the sages ask Brahmā who is the supreme god; Brahmā answers Kṛṣṇa/Govinda; then 'te hocuḥ kiṃ tadrūpam …', with the meditation form (gopaveṣam abhrābhaṃ taruṇaṃ kalpadrumāśritam; satpuṇḍarīkanayanam …) and the mantra. The e-text divides the pūrva into two upaniṣats.

paraphrase: Devotion is worship of him: fixing the mind on him with no desire for this world or the next; this alone is freedom from action (naiṣkarmya).

original.text: bhaktir asya bhajanaṃ tad ihāmutropādhinairāśyenaivāmuṣmin manaḥkalpanam etad eva ca naiṣkarmyam
